newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish president to visit Slovenia.
newsitem.headline: Polish president to visit Slovenia.

text.p: Polish President Aleksander Kwasniewski on Tuesday begins a two-day official visit to Slovenia aimed in part at correcting his country's unfavourable trade balance with the Alpine republic.
He will be accompanied by Foreign Trade Minister Jacek Buchacz and nine Polish business representatives, Kwasniewski foreign policy aide Zdzislaw Rapacki told a news conference on Monday.

Rapacki said total trade turnover between the two countries rose by 20 percent to $142.3 million in 1995, of which Slovene exports, dominated by pharmaceuticals and chemicals, amounted to about $105 million.
"This visit will be an occasion to create a better climate for economic cooperation," Rapacki said.

Kwasniewski and Slovene President Milan Kucan are due to issue a joint declaration on Wednesday stating the need for their countries to sign a planned agreement on cooperation and good neighbourly relations.
Kwasniewski's delegation includes Interior Minister Zbigniew Siemiatkowski, who will sign two bilateral agreements including one on fighting organised crime.
